Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Siemens ROX II xz-as-cat arbitrary disclosure of shadow/private keys (CVE-2025-40948) · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Siemens ROX II feature-key gpgv command injection to root (CVE-2025-40947) · [LLM] Siemens ROX II three-stage zero-day chain temporal correlation (CVE-2025-40948/40947/40949) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Siemens ROX II root cron persistence via web task scheduler (CVE-2025-40949) · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Three Steps to the Terminal: A Siemens ROX II Zero-Day Trilogy
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Siemens ROX II xz-as-cat arbitrary disclosure of shadow/private keys (CVE-2025-40948) AIReconnaissance Medium
Hunts the CVE-2025-40948 stage where a root-privileged xz utility is misused with decompress-to-stdout flags to read sensitive files (/etc/shadow, SSH/TLS private keys, config) on a Ruggedcom ROX II OT switch. Article-specific: xz functioning like cat against credential-bearing files is the reconnaissance foothold of the chain. Rationale: Uses the article's exact CVE-2025-40948 mechanic — root-privileged xz used like cat (decompress-to-stdout) against password hashes and private keys. Pairing xz with a sensitive-file target and a stdout/decompress flag makes it high-fidelity; xz legitimately never streams /etc/shadow. Cross-checked NVD and CISA ICSA-26-134-02. Cross-checked against: • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-40947 • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/ics-advisories/icsa-26-134-02 • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/siemens-rox-ii-zero-day-vulnerabilities/
ATT&CKT1003.008 T1552.004 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate admin decompressing a .xz log/backup archive with xz -dc to a pager
  • Firmware/update tooling that pipes xz -d output during a package install
  • A monitoring script that reads a config file that happens to end in .key but is not a private key
  • Backup jobs streaming compressed archives from /etc via xz
Suppression filter
| where not (SyslogMessage has_any ("backup","firmware","/var/log/") and not SyslogMessage has_any ("/etc/shadow","id_rsa","id_dsa","ssl/private"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full Syslog/auditd EXECVE line — confirm the xz target is /etc/shadow, an SSH/TLS private key, or a credential config, and identify the invoking user/session on the ROX II switch. 2) Contain: isolate the switch's management plane (block untrusted access to the web/CLI mgmt VLAN), rotate any exposed device keys/passwords, and confirm firmware is upgraded to V2.17.1. 3) Hunt: on the same device look for the follow-on chain — feature-key command injection (CVE-2025-40947) and root crontab modification (CVE-2025-40949) within the following minutes.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ProcessName has "xz" or SyslogMessage has "xz"
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("/etc/shadow","id_rsa","id_dsa","ssl/private",".pem",".key")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("--decompress","-dc"," -d ","--stdout","-c ")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, ProcessName, SyslogMessage, Facility, SeverityLevel
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Siemens ROX II feature-key gpgv command injection to root (CVE-2025-40947) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts CVE-2025-40947: an attacker-controlled feature-key payload submitted to the ROX II web/CLI management is inserted unsanitized into a root-privileged command, allowing shell command injection. Article-specific: feature-key validation input carrying shell metacharacters is the privilege-escalation pivot of the chain. Rationale: Grounded in the CVE-2025-40947 description — an unsanitized feature-key payload inserted directly into a root command. Detecting shell metacharacters (;, |, &&, $(), backtick, $IFS) inside a feature-key request/log line is high-fidelity because a legitimate feature key is an opaque signed token with no shell syntax. Corroborated via NVD and CISA ICSA-26-134-02. Cross-checked against: • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-40947 • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/ics-advisories/icsa-26-134-02
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1548
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Admin pasting a legitimate feature key that coincidentally contains a semicolon-delimited field
  • WAF/proxy URL-decoding artifacts that surface encoded characters in benign query strings
  • Automated inventory tooling querying the feature-key endpoint without injection payloads
  • Penetration-test / vulnerability-scanner traffic fuzzing the mgmt interface
Suppression filter
| where not (SyslogMessage has_any ("scanner","nessus","qualys") or ProcessName has_any ("nessus","scan"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: reconstruct the feature-key request/log entry — confirm shell metacharacters are inside the attacker-controlled key field rather than a benign token, and identify the authenticated user and source IP. 2) Contain: revoke the session, restrict the ROX II management interface to a trusted jump host, and verify firmware V2.17.1 is applied (the fix). 3) Hunt: check for a preceding CVE-2025-40948 xz file read and a following CVE-2025-40949 root crontab write on the same device to confirm full-chain execution; capture any commands spawned as root.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where SyslogMessage has "feature" and SyslogMessage has "key"
| where SyslogMessage contains "$(" or SyslogMessage contains "&&" or SyslogMessage contains "`" or SyslogMessage contains ";" or SyslogMessage contains "| " or SyslogMessage contains "$IFS"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, ProcessName, SyslogMessage, Facility, SeverityLevel
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:linux.syslog "feature-key" (";sh" OR "&&" OR "|sh" OR "|bash" OR "$IFS" OR "; /")
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*feature*key*" OR Web.uri_path="*featurekey*" OR Web.uri_path="*feature-key*") (Web.uri_query="*;*" OR Web.uri_query="*$(*" OR Web.uri_query="*|*" OR Web.uri_query="*&&*" OR Web.uri_query="*%3B*" OR Web.uri_query="*%24%28*" OR Web.uri_query="*%60*" OR Web.url="*%3B*" OR Web.url="*%24%28*") by Web.src Web.dest Web.url Web.uri_query Web.http_user_agent Web.http_method | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*feature*key*" OR Web.uri_path="*featurekey*" OR Web.uri_path="*feature-key*") (Web.uri_query="*;*" OR Web.uri_query="*$(*" OR Web.uri_query="*|*" OR Web.uri_query="*&&*" OR Web.uri_query="*%3B*" OR Web.uri_query="*%24%28*" OR Web.uri_query="*%60*" OR Web.url="*%3B*" OR Web.url="*%24%28*") by Web.src Web.dest Web.url Web.uri_query Web.http_user_agent Web.http_method | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Siemens ROX II root cron persistence via web task scheduler (CVE-2025-40949) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts CVE-2025-40949: an authenticated attacker abuses the ROX II web management task scheduler to inject commands into the root crontab, establishing reboot-surviving persistence. Article-specific: new root cron entries executing network-fetch or /tmp payloads are the persistence stage of the chain. Rationale: Maps to the CVE-2025-40949 mechanic — injected commands in the root cron table via the web scheduler. Cron parentage plus a remote-fetch/shell payload is high-fidelity: legitimate ROX II cron jobs do not curl/wget from /tmp or spawn reverse shells. Corroborated via NVD and CISA ICSA-26-134-02. Cross-checked against: • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-40947 • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/ics-advisories/icsa-26-134-02
ATT&CKT1053.003 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate scheduled maintenance job that uses curl/wget to pull an update from an internal server
  • Vendor diagnostic cron task writing to /tmp
  • Admin-created backup cron entry piping data out via a shell
  • Config-management agent (e.g. an internal orchestration script) launched from cron
Suppression filter
| where not (SyslogMessage has_any ("/opt/siemens/","internal-update") and RemoteHostAllowlisted == true)
Response runbook
1) Triage: dump the current root crontab and the ROX II task-scheduler audit entry — confirm the offending job was created via the web scheduler and points at an external host or /tmp payload. 2) Contain: remove the malicious cron entry, kill any spawned payload process, isolate the switch's mgmt plane, and upgrade to firmware V2.17.1. 3) Hunt: correlate backward to the CVE-2025-40947 feature-key injection and CVE-2025-40948 xz disclosure on the same device, and sweep other ROX II switches for identical cron entries or callback destinations.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Facility =~ "cron" or ProcessName has_any ("crontab","crond","CRON")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("wget","curl","/tmp/","bash -i","/dev/tcp/","base64 -d","nc ") or SyslogMessage contains "$("
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, ProcessName, Facility, SyslogMessage, SeverityLevel
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: Detects cron-launched processes fetching remote payloads or executing shells, consistent with the CVE-2025-40949 root crontab injection stage on Siemens Ruggedcom ROX II.

ENDPOINT

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name=cron OR Processes.parent_process_name=crond OR Processes.parent_process_name=CRON) (Processes.process="*wget*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*/tmp/*" OR Processes.process="*bash -i*" OR Processes.process="*nc *" OR Processes.process="*/dev/tcp/*" OR Processes.process="*base64 -d*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)

Siemens ROX II three-stage zero-day chain temporal correlation (CVE-2025-40948/40947/40949) AIExploitation High
Correlates the three chained ROX II exploit stages — xz file disclosure, feature-key command injection, and root cron persistence — observed on the same switch within a short window. Article-specific: alerts on the documented 'three steps to the terminal' progression rather than any single stage in isolation. Rationale: Encodes the article's core thesis — the 'three steps to the terminal' chain — by requiring ≥2 distinct documented stages (xz disclosure, feature-key injection, root cron persistence) on one ROX II switch within a 10-minute bin, which is far higher-fidelity than any single-stage alert. Datadog query surfaces the indicators; the count/window is applied at rule level. Corroborated via NVD and CISA ICSA-26-134-02. Cross-checked against: • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-40947 • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/ics-advisories/icsa-26-134-02
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1053.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized penetration test replaying the full chain against a lab ROX II
  • Vendor validation run of the V2.17.1 patch that exercises xz, feature-key and scheduler code paths
  • Noisy vulnerability scanner touching all three mgmt endpoints in one sweep
  • A single benign admin session that legitimately reads a config, sets a feature key, and edits a cron job in quick succession
Suppression filter
| where not (Computer has_any ("lab","test","staging") or HostIP in ("127.0.0.1"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: open the correlated evidence set and confirm the stages are attacker-driven (sensitive-file xz read, metacharacters in feature-key, remote/tmp cron payload) rather than benign admin work; identify the switch, user and source IP. 2) Contain: isolate the switch management plane, revoke the session, remove any malicious cron entry, rotate exposed device credentials/keys, and enforce firmware V2.17.1. 3) Hunt: pivot on the source IP and callback destinations across all ROX II / Ruggedcom devices for identical chain activity and stage-3 persistence artifacts.
let Window = 10m;
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| extend Stage = case(
    SyslogMessage has "xz" and SyslogMessage has_any("/etc/shadow","id_rsa","id_dsa","ssl/private",".pem",".key"), "1-disclosure",
    (SyslogMessage has "feature" and SyslogMessage has "key") and (SyslogMessage contains "$(" or SyslogMessage contains "&&" or SyslogMessage contains ";" or SyslogMessage contains "`" or SyslogMessage contains "$IFS"), "2-cmdinjection",
    (ProcessName has_any ("cron","crond","crontab") or Facility =~ "cron") and (SyslogMessage has_any("wget","curl","/tmp/","/dev/tcp/","base64 -d") or SyslogMessage contains "$("), "3-persistence",
    "")
| where isnotempty(Stage)

ACR Stealer Uses ClickFix Lures to Steal Browser Tokens and Microsoft 365 Files

The Hacker News
2026-07-17 19 use cases 8 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

ACR Stealer, an infostealer in circulation since 2024, is walking out of enterprise networks with saved browser passwords, live session tokens, PDFs, Microsoft 365 documents, and files from synced OneDrive and SharePoint folders. It gets in because someone pasted a command into a Run box and pressed Enter. Microsoft laid out two of the delivery chains on Thursday. Its Defender Experts team, the

ClickFix Run-dialog paste writes mshta/rundll32/pushd command to Explorer RunMRU AIDelivery High
Hunts the ClickFix initial-access step where a victim pastes an attacker-supplied command into the Windows Run box; the shell records it under HKCU\...\Explorer\RunMRU. Fires when that recorded command contains the LOLBins ACR Stealer's chains use (mshta, rundll32, pushd, conhost) or a remote/UNC target. Rationale: RunMRU is the definitive fingerprint of a Run-box paste, and pairing it with the article's exact LOLBins (mshta, rundll32, pushd, conhost) plus a remote/UNC target makes it ClickFix-specific rather than generic autorun noise. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/07/16/acr-stealer-two-observed-intrusion-chains-amid-increased-threat-activity/ • https://isc.sans.edu/diary/33018 • https://www.lindensec.com/post/dissecting-a-live-clickfix-attack-etherhiding-webdav-abuse-and-how-asr-saves-the-day
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1112
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Power users legitimately launching cmd/powershell from the Run box for admin work
  • IT scripts distributed by helpdesk telling users to paste a benign diagnostic command
  • Software vendors documenting a 'paste this into Run' install workaround
  • Automated GPO/logon scripts that seed RunMRU on imaged machines
  • Developers testing rundll32/mshta invocations locally
Suppression filter
| where RegistryValueData has_any ("\\\\","http://","https://","mshta","rundll32","pushd","conhost") and not (RegistryValueData has_any ("\\\\corp\\","\\\\dfs\\") and InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "explorer.exe" and InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("helpdesk","svc-imaging"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full RegistryValueData and resolve any http/UNC target; check whether the same host then spawned mshta.exe or rundll32.exe within minutes (join DeviceProcessEvents on DeviceId). 2) Contain: if a remote HTA or WebDAV DLL load followed, isolate the host, kill mshta/rundll32/pythonw, and revoke the signed-in user's session tokens (not just password). 3) Hunt: sweep the org for the same RunMRU string and for outbound connections to the ACR campaign domains; check for the pythonw.exe/scheduled-task persistence artifacts.
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType == "RegistryValueSet"
| where RegistryKey has @"\Explorer\RunMRU"
| where RegistryValueData has_any ("mshta","rundll32","powershell","pwsh","pushd","conhost","curl","http","\\\\")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where RegistryKey has @"\Explorer\RunMRU"
| where RegistryValueData has_any ("mshta","rundll32","powershell","pwsh","pushd","conhost","curl","http","\\")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

mshta.exe fileless chain: remote HTA fetch then in-memory PowerShell with TLS-validation bypass AIExploitation High
Hunts ACR Stealer's fileless chain where the pasted command spawns mshta.exe to pull remote HTA content, whose VBScript loader fires PowerShell that disables certificate validation and runs a JPEG-carried payload in memory. Anchors on mshta.exe invoking a remote URL/.hta and flags the .NET cert-bypass strings when present. Rationale: mshta.exe fetching a remote HTA is the documented fileless entry point; the cert-bypass strings (ServicePointManager.ServerCertificateValidationCallback) are searched inside ProcessCommandLine as enrichment, not treated as schema columns, fixing the prior validation error. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/07/16/acr-stealer-two-observed-intrusion-chains-amid-increased-threat-activity/ • https://isc.sans.edu/diary/33018
ATT&CKT1218.005 T1059.001 T1027.011
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legacy internal LOB apps still delivered as HTA from an intranet URL
  • Vendor tooling that shells mshta against an internal http endpoint
  • Admin troubleshooting scripts using mshta with a local file (excluded by http/.hta filter)
  • Security-tool self-tests / atomic red team runs
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://intranet","https://intranet",".corp.local") and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("iexplore.exe","explorer.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: extract the remote URL, resolve it, and check DeviceNetworkEvents for the follow-on JPEG pull from an image host; look for a PowerShell child of this mshta with the cert-bypass strings. 2) Contain: isolate the host, terminate mshta/powershell, and revoke the user's browser session tokens since credential theft runs in-memory. 3) Hunt: pivot on the image-host domain and on any host that resolved it; check for Chrome/Edge 'Login Data'/'Web Data' access by non-browser processes.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "mshta.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://",".hta")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| extend CertBypass = ProcessCommandLine has_any ("ServerCertificateValidationCallback","CheckCertificateRevocation","ServicePointManager")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, CertBypass
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("http://","https://",".hta")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| extend CertBypass = CommandLine has_any ("ServerCertificateValidationCallback","CheckCertificateRevocation","ServicePointManager")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, CertBypass
| order by TimeGenerated desc

rundll32.exe loading a DLL from a WebDAV/UNC share by ordinal export AIInstallation High
Hunts the disk-leaving ACR Stealer chain that runs rundll32.exe against a DLL pulled from a remote WebDAV share (GUID directory, fake extension like .google) and invoked by ordinal (,#1). Matches rundll32 with a UNC path plus an ordinal-export invocation, and the named host sphere-api.dialectosphere.in.net. Rationale: rundll32 loading a DLL by ordinal from a UNC/WebDAV path is exactly Red Canary's / Microsoft's documented example command; the ordinal-export regex plus the named host sphere-api.dialectosphere.in.net make this high-fidelity and low-FP. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/07/16/acr-stealer-two-observed-intrusion-chains-amid-increased-threat-activity/ • https://redcanary.com/blog/threat-intelligence/intelligence-insights-may-2026/ • https://isc.sans.edu/diary/33018
ATT&CKT1218.011 T1570 T1071.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Enterprise software that legitimately runs a DLL from a signed internal DFS/UNC share
  • Deployment tooling (SCCM/Intune) invoking rundll32 against a network path
  • Printer/driver installers referencing UNC resources
  • Backup/AV agents loading helper DLLs from a mapped drive
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("\\\\corp\\","\\\\dfs.","\\\\fileserver") and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("ccmexec.exe","msiexec.exe","services.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: resolve the UNC host in the command line; confirm it is external (not a corp DFS/file server) and check DeviceNetworkEvents for the WebDAV connection over 443. 2) Contain: isolate the host, block the remote host at proxy/firewall, terminate rundll32, and revoke the user's tokens. 3) Hunt: search for the same GUID-directory pattern and fake extensions (.google/.ct) org-wide, plus pushd usage mounting a remote share and conhost.exe --headless wrappers.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "rundll32.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "\\\\"
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i),\s*#?\d+"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| extend NamedHost = ProcessCommandLine has_any ("sphere-api.dialectosphere.in.net",".google,",".ct,")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, NamedHost
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\rundll32.exe"
| where CommandLine contains "\\\\"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i),\s*#?\d+"
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

conhost.exe --headless wrapping pushd/rundll32 (ClickFix console-hiding variant) AIInstallation High
Hunts the stealthiest ACR Stealer variant that wraps its WebDAV rundll32 execution in conhost.exe --headless to suppress the console window, mounting the remote share with pushd and hiding strings behind delayed environment-variable expansion. Anchors on the rare conhost --headless flag alongside pushd/rundll32/UNC content. Rationale: conhost.exe --headless is an uncommon flag that Microsoft specifically calls out as the stealthiest ACR variant's console-hiding trick; pairing it with pushd/rundll32/UNC content in the same or parent command line removes benign headless-console noise. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/07/16/acr-stealer-two-observed-intrusion-chains-amid-increased-threat-activity/ • https://www.cyberproof.com/blog/the-clickfix-evolution-new-variant-replaces-powershell-with-rundll32-and-webdav/
ATT&CKT1564.003 T1218.011 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Windows Terminal / modern console host spawning conhost with new flags during updates
  • Developer tooling invoking conhost --headless for pseudo-console (ConPTY) automation
  • CI/build agents using headless consoles
  • Terminal-emulator apps embedding conhost
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("windowsterminal.exe","wt.exe","code.exe","devenv.exe") )
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the parent command line and expand any delayed-expansion (%var%) strings to reveal the hidden pushd/rundll32/host. 2) Contain: isolate the host, terminate the conhost/rundll32 tree, and revoke the user's session tokens. 3) Hunt: search for pushd mounting remote shares, the WebDAV DLL-load pattern, and follow-on pythonw.exe execution from %LocalAppData%\Temp on the same host.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "conhost.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "--headless"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("pushd","rundll32","cmd","\\\\") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("pushd","rundll32","--headless")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\conhost.exe"
| where CommandLine has "--headless"
| where CommandLine has_any ("pushd","rundll32","cmd","\\\\")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

pythonw.exe silently running a script from %LocalAppData%\Temp (LogiOptionsPlus lure) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the second-stage ACR loader: obfuscated PowerShell drops a ZIP into a folder under %LocalAppData%\Temp with an innocuous name (e.g. LogiOptionsPlus) and a bundled pythonw.exe launches the Python script so nothing appears on screen. Anchors on pythonw.exe running a .py from an AppData\Local\Temp path spawned by a script host. Rationale: pythonw.exe (no console) running a script out of %LocalAppData%\Temp under an innocuous folder name and spawned by PowerShell is the exact stealthy loader Microsoft describes; LogiOptionsPlus is the named decoy folder used as a strong anchor. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/07/16/acr-stealer-two-observed-intrusion-chains-amid-increased-threat-activity/ • https://www.lindensec.com/post/dissecting-a-live-clickfix-attack-etherhiding-webdav-abuse-and-how-asr-saves-the-day
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1204.002 T1564.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Python apps that bundle pythonw and run scripts from a per-user temp/cache dir
  • Data-science tooling launching pythonw from AppData
  • Packaged Electron/Python installers unpacking to Temp on first run
  • Developer venv activity under the user profile
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("pip.exe","conda.exe","code.exe") or FolderPath has_any ("\\Programs\\Python\\","\\Anaconda3\\"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: locate the .py path and the parent ZIP under %LocalAppData%\Temp; confirm the parent was obfuscated PowerShell, and check whether the installer wiped prior copies (updater behavior). 2) Contain: isolate the host, terminate pythonw, remove the scheduled task, and revoke tokens. 3) Hunt: look for the second Python loader making outbound connections to blockchain RPC/Web3 endpoints (EtherHiding) and for the timestomp/PS-history-clear persistence markers.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "pythonw.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (".py","LogiOptionsPlus")
| where FolderPath has @"\AppData\Local\" or ProcessCommandLine has @"AppData\Local\Temp" or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\pythonw.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any (".py","LogiOptionsPlus")
| where CommandLine has @"AppData\Local\Temp" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\powershell.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\pwsh.exe"
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Hidden scheduled task masquerading as a software update, created by a script host AIInstallation Medium
Hunts ACR Stealer's persistence: a hidden scheduled task posing as a software update, created not by a legitimate installer but by powershell/python/cmd. Anchors on schtasks.exe /create with update-themed task names and a script-host or pythonw parent. Rationale: The differentiator from benign updaters is the parent: legit update tasks are registered by installers/services, not by powershell/python/mshta/rundll32; combined with update-themed naming this isolates ACR's masquerading persistence. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/07/16/acr-stealer-two-observed-intrusion-chains-amid-increased-threat-activity/
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Admins scripting scheduled-task creation via PowerShell for genuine patch jobs
  • Configuration-management tools (Ansible/DSC) that create update tasks from a shell
  • Third-party updater frameworks that self-register via a wrapper script
  • Software packaging during app deployment
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Ansible","DesiredStateConfiguration","Intune") or InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("svc-patch","svc-sccm"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: dump the task's action (schtasks /query /tn <name> /xml) to reveal the payload path — check for pythonw/rundll32 and hidden window flags. 2) Contain: delete the task, isolate the host, terminate the payload process, and revoke user tokens. 3) Hunt: correlate with timestamp copying off notepad.exe (timestomp) and Microsoft-PowerShell/Operational history clearing on the same host, and sweep the org for identically named tasks.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/create"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("update","Update","LogiOptions","OneDrive")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","pythonw.exe","python.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\schtasks.exe"
| where CommandLine has "/create"
| where CommandLine has_any ("update","Update","LogiOptions","OneDrive")
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","pythonw.exe","python.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Python loader making EtherHiding calls to blockchain RPC / Web3 node infrastructure AICommand & Control Low
Hunts the EtherHiding C2 stage where a second Python loader queries public blockchain RPC endpoints / Web3 node infrastructure to pull a payload or C2 address off a public ledger. Anchors on python/pythonw.exe reaching public Web3/RPC hosts — no attacker-controlled resolver to seize, so process-to-blockchain egress is the signal. Rationale: Microsoft explicitly names EtherHiding via a second Python loader talking to public blockchain RPC/Web3 nodes; the article gives no fixed domains, so this is scoped to python(w).exe reaching Web3/RPC hostnames and shipped as Low-confidence hunting — validate hits against the campaign process tree. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/07/16/acr-stealer-two-observed-intrusion-chains-amid-increased-threat-activity/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/clickfix-campaign-uses-etherhiding-and-guloader/
ATT&CKT1102 T1071.001 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate blockchain/crypto developers running Python Web3 clients (web3.py) on corporate hosts
  • Data engineers pulling on-chain data via python scripts
  • Trading/analytics tools that query public RPC nodes
  • Wallet or dApp automation on developer workstations
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("\\Programs\\Python\\","\\Anaconda3\\","\\venv\\") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "web3.py")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the initiating pythonw.exe came from %LocalAppData%\Temp (not a dev venv) and correlate with the ClickFix process tree on the same host. 2) Contain: isolate the host, terminate python(w), and treat the user's tokens/creds as compromised (revoke, not rotate). 3) Hunt: capture the RPC hostname/contract queried, block it, and check whether the resolved payload/C2 led to browser credential-store access or M365 file collection.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("pythonw.exe","python.exe")

Non-browser process touching Chrome/Edge 'Login Data' and 'Web Data' credential stores AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts ACR Stealer's credential-access step: reading Chrome/Edge Login Data and Web Data SQLite DBs and invoking DPAPI to decrypt saved passwords, cookies, and tokens. Fires when a process other than the browser itself creates/copies/accesses these exact files under the browser User Data path. Rationale: The article's verbatim code blocks name 'Login Data' and 'Web Data' as the exact SQLite DBs ACR reads before DPAPI decryption; a non-browser process touching those files under the browser User Data path is a high-fidelity credential-theft signal. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/07/16/acr-stealer-two-observed-intrusion-chains-amid-increased-threat-activity/ • https://redcanary.com/blog/threat-intelligence/intelligence-insights-may-2026/
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1539 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Backup or endpoint-DLP agents indexing the user profile
  • Browser sync/migration utilities and password-manager importers
  • Antivirus/EDR file scanners reading the DB (usually excluded above)
  • Enterprise browser-management tooling reading profile data
  • Chrome/Edge helper processes with a renamed image
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("code42service.exe","crashplanservice.exe","backup.exe","1password.exe","keepass.exe","dlpagent.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the accessing process image/path and hash; confirm it is not a sanctioned backup/DLP agent and check its parent chain back to mshta/rundll32/pythonw. 2) Contain: isolate the host and IMMEDIATELY revoke the user's browser session tokens and M365 refresh tokens (passwords rotate is insufficient per Microsoft guidance). 3) Hunt: check for exfil of the copied DB and for OneDrive/SharePoint/PDF collection on the same host; force sign-out of all sessions for the affected identity.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Web Data","Cookies")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data", @"\BraveSoftware\")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","explorer.exe","searchindexer.exe","onedrive.exe","msmpeng.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Web Data","Cookies")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data", @"\BraveSoftware\")
| where not(ActingProcessName has_any ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","explorer.exe","onedrive.exe"))
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Non-Browser Access to Chrome/Edge Login Data and Web Data
id: d4b1e097-8a6c-4f23-9b70-2e5c1a0f39b8
status: experimental
description: Detects a non-browser process touching Chrome/Edge Login Data or Web Data credential databases, matching ACR Stealer browser-token theft.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/acr-stealer-uses-clickfix-lures-to.html
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/07/16/acr-stealer-two-observed-intrusion-chains-amid-increased-threat-activity/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/17
tags:
  - attack.t1555.003
  - attack.t1539
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\Google\Chrome\User Data'
      - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data'
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\Login Data'
      - '\Web Data'
      - '\Cookies'
  filter_browser:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
      - '\brave.exe'
      - '\explorer.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_browser
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\\Login\ Data OR *\\Web\ Data OR *\\Cookies) @TargetFilename:(*\\Chrome\\User\ Data* OR *\\Edge\\User\ Data* OR *\\BraveSoftware*) -@Image:(*\\chrome.exe OR *\\msedge.exe OR *\\brave.exe OR *\\explorer.exe OR *\\CHROME.EXE OR *\\MSEDGE.EXE)
#event_simpleName=/^(FileOpenInfo|FileWritten)$/ TargetFileName=/\\(Login Data|Web Data|Cookies)$/i
| regex("\\\\(Chrome|Edge|BraveSoftware)\\\\User Data", field=TargetFileName, flags="i")
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(chrome|msedge|brave|opera|explorer|onedrive)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="Login Data" OR Filesystem.file_name="Web Data" OR Filesystem.file_name="Cookies") (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Google\\Chrome\\User Data*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Microsoft\\Edge\\User Data*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\BraveSoftware\\*") Filesystem.process_name!=chrome.exe Filesystem.process_name!=msedge.exe Filesystem.process_name!=brave.exe by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="Login Data" OR Filesystem.file_name="Web Data" OR Filesystem.file_name="Cookies") (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Google\\Chrome\\User Data*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Microsoft\\Edge\\User Data*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\BraveSoftware\\*") Filesystem.process_name!=chrome.exe Filesystem.process_name!=msedge.exe Filesystem.process_name!=brave.exe by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Endpoint beaconing to ACR Stealer ClickFix campaign payload-host / C2 domains AICommand & Control High
Hunts network connections to the corroborated ACR Stealer campaign infrastructure (payload hosts and C2), including creativecommunityinfo.art, enhanceblabber.cc, sphere-api.dialectosphere.in.net and the .icu/.sale rotation set. Straight IOC match for confirmed campaign domains. Rationale: These are the campaign domains cross-confirmed between Microsoft's Campaign 2 table (creativecommunityinfo.art payload host, enhanceblabber.cc C2), Brad Duncan's SANS diary (sphere-api.dialectosphere.in.net), and Red Canary (claude-desktop.gitlab.io) — direct IOC matches with negligible legitimate traffic. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/07/16/acr-stealer-two-observed-intrusion-chains-amid-increased-threat-activity/ • https://isc.sans.edu/diary/33018 • https://redcanary.com/blog/threat-intelligence/intelligence-insights-may-2026/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researchers/sandboxes deliberately resolving the IOCs
  • Threat-intel enrichment tooling pre-resolving domains for scoring
  • DNS sinkhole/telemetry appliances logging blocked lookups as 'queries'
  • Stale browser tabs re-resolving a since-seized domain
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("nslookup.exe","dig.exe") and InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("svc-threatintel","soc-analyst"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the initiating process and whether resolution succeeded/connected; because domains rotate, treat any hit as high-priority and pull the host's full process tree. 2) Contain: block the domains and resolved IPs at proxy/DNS/firewall, isolate the host, and revoke the user's tokens. 3) Hunt: pivot to the resolved IP for co-hosted rotation domains, and sweep for the ClickFix RunMRU / rundll32-WebDAV / pythonw markers on any host that queried these.
let iocs = dynamic(["creativecommunityinfo.art","enhanceblabber.cc","sphere-api.dialectosphere.in.net","claude-desktop.gitlab.io","deep-harborio.com","auramatrixa.com","zealpraxis.com","prism-vertex.com","prism-matrixs.com","proton-network.com","fairpoint29.com","primemetricsa.com","looksta.icu","quirksturdy.icu","strainedeasily.icu","wifihot.icu","filloco.icu","raidher.icu","apigrokcloud.icu","cpppemwjewjoiwejow.sale"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (iocs)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let iocs = dynamic(["creativecommunityinfo.art","enhanceblabber.cc","sphere-api.dialectosphere.in.net","claude-desktop.gitlab.io","deep-harborio.com","auramatrixa.com","zealpraxis.com","prism-vertex.com","prism-matrixs.com","proton-network.com","fairpoint29.com","primemetricsa.com","looksta.icu","quirksturdy.icu","strainedeasily.icu","wifihot.icu","filloco.icu","raidher.icu","apigrokcloud.icu","cpppemwjewjoiwejow.sale"]);
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DnsQuery has_any (iocs)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("70b5ecc110e074dbca92932c0e840ea3492ea0a43c3f215b71392c12b02213b2", "a14c3ecf5eb3d2543358482e43dc765dbf9ee7a4bec7571f5ecb8829ca719692", "47fa746422f1bf6b7712dc6803378e6a995488007193a7441d790f70d204728f") or SHA1 in~ ("70b5ecc110e074dbca92932c0e840ea3492ea0a43c3f215b71392c12b02213b2", "a14c3ecf5eb3d2543358482e43dc765dbf9ee7a4bec7571f5ecb8829ca719692", "47fa746422f1bf6b7712dc6803378e6a995488007193a7441d790f70d204728f") or MD5 in~ ("70b5ecc110e074dbca92932c0e840ea3492ea0a43c3f215b71392c12b02213b2", "a14c3ecf5eb3d2543358482e43dc765dbf9ee7a4bec7571f5ecb8829ca719692", "47fa746422f1bf6b7712dc6803378e6a995488007193a7441d790f70d204728f")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("70b5ecc110e074dbca92932c0e840ea3492ea0a43c3f215b71392c12b02213b2", "a14c3ecf5eb3d2543358482e43dc765dbf9ee7a4bec7571f5ecb8829ca719692", "47fa746422f1bf6b7712dc6803378e6a995488007193a7441d790f70d204728f") or SHA1 in~ ("70b5ecc110e074dbca92932c0e840ea3492ea0a43c3f215b71392c12b02213b2", "a14c3ecf5eb3d2543358482e43dc765dbf9ee7a4bec7571f5ecb8829ca719692", "47fa746422f1bf6b7712dc6803378e6a995488007193a7441d790f70d204728f") or MD5 in~ ("70b5ecc110e074dbca92932c0e840ea3492ea0a43c3f215b71392c12b02213b2", "a14c3ecf5eb3d2543358482e43dc765dbf9ee7a4bec7571f5ecb8829ca719692", "47fa746422f1bf6b7712dc6803378e6a995488007193a7441d790f70d204728f")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["70b5ecc110e074dbca92932c0e840ea3492ea0a43c3f215b71392c12b02213b2", "a14c3ecf5eb3d2543358482e43dc765dbf9ee7a4bec7571f5ecb8829ca719692", "47fa746422f1bf6b7712dc6803378e6a995488007193a7441d790f70d204728f"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

ACR Stealer: Two observed intrusion chains amid increased threat activity

Microsoft Security Blog
2026-07-16 18 use cases 12 techniques 7 kill-chain phases detected

From late April 2026 to mid-June 2026, Microsoft Defender Experts observed increased ACR Stealer activity across customer environments. These campaigns are successfully using ClickFix lures to steal browser credentials, authentication tokens, and sensitive documents from enterprise environments. The post ACR Stealer: Two observed intrusion chains amid increased threat activity appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] ClickFix RunMRU entry launching rundll32 against WebDAV GUID share (ACR Stealer) · [LLM] MSHTA remote HTA launched by explorer→powershell chain (ACR Stealer fileless campaign) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — ACR Stealer: Two observed intrusion chains amid increased threat activity
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] rundll32 loading DLL from remote WebDAV @ssl GUID share with ordinal export (ACR Stealer) · [LLM] Masqueraded 'Autoupdate' scheduled task run by PowerShell loader (ACR Stealer persistence) · [LLM] pythonw.exe loader executing from deceptive %LocalAppData%\Temp dir (ACR Stealer) · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Endpoint traffic to ACR Stealer C2 / dead-drop domains · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
ClickFix RunMRU entry launching rundll32 against WebDAV GUID share (ACR Stealer) AIDelivery High
Hunts the ACR Stealer ClickFix initial-access artifact: a Run-dialog (RunMRU) history value in which the pasted command drives cmd.exe/rundll32.exe to load a DLL from a remote WebDAV share addressed as a `@ssl` UNC path with a GUID directory. This is the on-disk fingerprint left when a victim pastes the ClickFix command, before any child process runs. Rationale: Anchors on the article's Block 1 RunMRU logic plus the corroborated `@ssl\<GUID>\` WebDAV UNC form; RunMRU only records manually pasted Run-dialog commands, so rundll32+@ssl+GUID there is near-zero-FP evidence of ClickFix paste-execution. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.gridinsoft.com/acr-stealer-clickfix-attacks/ • https://www.csoonline.com/article/4198788/new-acr-stealer-campaigns-use-webdav-mshta-to-evade-detection.html
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1218.011 T1071.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Rare legitimate admin scripting that maps a WebDAV DAVWWWRoot share via rundll32 (uncommon in enterprise)
  • Security researcher / red team replaying the ClickFix chain in a sandbox
  • Backup or MDM tooling that writes synthetic RunMRU entries (very rare)
  • Manual analyst reproduction of the IOC on a triage box
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full RegistryValueData and extract the WebDAV host + GUID; confirm it matches sphere-api.dialectosphere.in.net or another external host, and check whether a rundll32.exe process with that UNC path actually spawned. 2) Contain: isolate the endpoint, block the WebDAV host/domain at proxy and DNS, and kill any rundll32/pythonw child processes. 3) Hunt: search the same host for the follow-on %LocalAppData%\Temp deceptive dir, the 'Autoupdate' scheduled task, and outbound traffic to the ACR C2 domains.
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RegistryKey has "RunMRU"
| where RegistryValueData has_all ("rundll32", "@ssl")
| where RegistryValueData matches regex @"(?i)@ssl\\[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}\\"
| where RegistryValueData has_any ("start", "pushd", ",#1", ".google")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where RegistryKey has "RunMRU"
| where RegistryValueData has_all ("rundll32", "@ssl")
| where RegistryValueData matches regex @"(?i)@ssl\\[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}\\"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: ACR Stealer ClickFix RunMRU rundll32 WebDAV Share
id: 3f9c1e2a-7b64-4c0d-9a11-4e6b2f8c5d10
description: Detects a RunMRU history value where the ClickFix command runs rundll32 against a WebDAV @ssl GUID share, as used by ACR Stealer campaign 1.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/07/16/acr-stealer-two-observed-intrusion-chains-amid-increased-threat-activity/
  - https://blog.gridinsoft.com/acr-stealer-clickfix-attacks/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/21
tags:
  - attack.t1204.004
  - attack.t1218.011
logsource:
  category: registry_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    RegistryKey|contains: 'RunMRU'
    RegistryValueData|contains|all:
      - 'rundll32'
      - '@ssl'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:13 (@TargetObject:(*\\RunMRU\\* OR *\\runmru\\*)) @Details:(*rundll32*@ssl* OR *RUNDLL32*@SSL*)
#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate RegObjectName=/RunMRU/i | regex("(?i)rundll32.*@ssl", field=RegStringValue) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RegStringValue], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `security_content_summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_key_name="*RunMRU*" (Registry.registry_value_data="*rundll32*" AND Registry.registry_value_data="*@ssl*") by Registry.dest Registry.registry_key_name Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_data Registry.process_id | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | regex registry_value_data="(?i)@ssl\\[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}\\" | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false `security_content_summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_key_name="*RunMRU*" (Registry.registry_value_data="*rundll32*" AND Registry.registry_value_data="*@ssl*") by Registry.dest Registry.registry_key_name Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_data Registry.process_id | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | regex registry_value_data="(?i)@ssl\\[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}\\" | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
rundll32 loading DLL from remote WebDAV @ssl GUID share with ordinal export (ACR Stealer) AIInstallation High
Hunts the ACR Stealer campaign-1 execution step where rundll32.exe loads a DLL directly from a remote WebDAV share (UNC `\\host@SSL\<GUID>\<name>.google,#1`) over HTTPS. Matches the exact confirmed sample cmdline against sphere-api.dialectosphere.in.net and the GUID directory + `,#1` ordinal export. Rationale: Uses the externally-confirmed exact cmdline shape (`rundll32.exe \\sphere-api.dialectosphere.in.net\<GUID>\...google,#1`): rundll32 loading a DLL over a WebDAV @ssl UNC with a GUID dir and `,#N` ordinal export is not seen in benign activity. Cross-checked against: • https://www.csoonline.com/article/4198788/new-acr-stealer-campaigns-use-webdav-mshta-to-evade-detection.html • https://blog.gridinsoft.com/acr-stealer-clickfix-attacks/
ATT&CKT1218.011 T1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Enterprise apps that legitimately load resources from a mapped WebDAV/DAVWWWRoot path via rundll32 (rare)
  • Penetration test or purple-team replay of the ACR chain
  • Software installer that side-loads a DLL from an internal SharePoint WebDAV mount (would lack the external GUID host)
  • EDR sensor telemetry replays during IR reproduction
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !endswith "$" and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msiexec.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the WebDAV host is external and non-corporate, capture the GUID path and DLL name, and check for a preceding cmd.exe/pushd parent and RunMRU paste. 2) Contain: isolate the host, block the WebDAV domain/IP at proxy+DNS, and terminate rundll32 and any spawned pythonw.exe. 3) Hunt: sweep the fleet for the same GUID host or `,#1` ordinal pattern, and for the LogiOptionsPlus temp dir and 'Autoupdate' scheduled task on affected hosts.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "rundll32.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i),#\d+\s*$"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "@ssl" or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("sphere-api.dialectosphere.in.net","creativecommunityinfo.art","enhanceblabber.cc","looksta.icu")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\rundll32.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i),#\d+\s*$"
| where (CommandLine has "@ssl" or CommandLine has_any ("sphere-api.dialectosphere.in.net","creativecommunityinfo.art","enhanceblabber.cc","looksta.icu"))
| where CommandLine matches regex @"[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

MSHTA remote HTA launched by explorer→powershell chain (ACR Stealer fileless campaign) AIDelivery High
Hunts the ACR Stealer campaign-2 fileless chain: explorer.exe spawns a bare powershell.exe which invokes mshta.exe against a remote HTTPS URL whose path is a 7-digit numeric token. Matches the article's exact process-tree and cmdline shape for the MSHTA/steganography route. Rationale: Directly implements the article's Block 3 process-tree (explorer→powershell→mshta) plus the remote HTTPS HTA with a 7-digit path token; mshta fetching a remote URL from a PowerShell parent is a strong LOLBin proxy-execution signal specific to this campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/acr-stealer-uses-clickfix-lures-to.html • https://www.csoonline.com/article/4198788/new-acr-stealer-campaigns-use-webdav-mshta-to-evade-detection.html
ATT&CKT1218.005 T1059.001 T1204.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legacy internal LOB app delivered as a remote HTA via a launcher script (rare, and usually internal host not HTTPS/7-digit path)
  • Red-team ClickFix simulation
  • Admin troubleshooting that manually runs mshta against a URL
  • IT automation using mshta for a hosted config page
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
1) Triage: extract the mshta URL, detonate/inspect it for the steganographic PNG stage, and confirm the explorer→powershell parentage indicates a paste-run rather than scripted automation. 2) Contain: isolate the host, block the HTA URL/domain, and kill mshta plus any in-memory child. 3) Hunt: look for follow-on obfuscated PowerShell, VirtualAlloc/Fiber-API in-memory execution, and browser credential-store access on the same host.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName has "explorer.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "powershell.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine in~ ('"PowerShell.exe" ', '"PowerShell.exe"')
| where FileName =~ "mshta.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "https://" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex "/[0-9]{7}"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\powershell.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine has "https://" and CommandLine matches regex "/[0-9]{7}"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Masqueraded 'Autoupdate' scheduled task run by PowerShell loader (ACR Stealer persistence) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the ACR Stealer campaign-1 persistence/updater behavior where the obfuscated PowerShell loader invokes schtasks to run a hidden task named 'Autoupdate' suffixed with an 8-digit numeric token, disguised as a legitimate software update triggering at user sign-in. Rationale: Implements the article's Block 2 exactly: a PowerShell parent driving schtasks against a task named 'Autoupdate' with an 8-digit token is a specific masqueraded-update persistence artifact, far narrower than generic scheduled-task creation. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/microsoft-warns-of-surge-in-acr-stealer-attacks-on-customers/
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1059.001 T1036
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate software updaters that create tasks literally named 'Autoupdate' via a PowerShell installer (check the parent chain and signer)
  • Endpoint management/RMM tooling scripting scheduled tasks named with build numbers
  • Internal packaging scripts that name update tasks with date-stamps (8 digits)
  • Admin manually registering an update task through a PS console
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !endswith "$" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("AppData\\Local\\Temp", "pythonw", "LogiOptionsPlus")
Response runbook
1) Triage: dump the full schtasks cmdline and the task action/trigger; confirm the action points to pythonw.exe or a %LocalAppData%\Temp path rather than a signed vendor binary. 2) Contain: delete the malicious task, isolate the host, and kill the associated pythonw/loader process. 3) Hunt: correlate to the upstream rundll32 WebDAV load and RunMRU paste, and check other hosts for identically-named 'Autoupdate'+8-digit tasks pointing into Temp.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "powershell.exe"
| where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_all ("schtasks", "/tn", "Autoupdate")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex "[0-9]{8}"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\powershell.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\schtasks.exe"
| where CommandLine has_all ("/tn", "Autoupdate")
| where CommandLine matches regex "[0-9]{8}"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

pythonw.exe loader executing from deceptive %LocalAppData%\Temp dir (ACR Stealer) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the ACR Stealer campaign-1 install step where a ZIP payload is extracted into a deceptive folder under %LocalAppData%\Temp (e.g. LogiOptionsPlus) and a bundled pythonw.exe is launched from that path by a PowerShell/cmd parent to run the obfuscated Python stealer loader with no console window. Rationale: Anchors on the article's install behavior: a bundled pythonw.exe run from a deceptive %LocalAppData%\Temp dir (e.g. LogiOptionsPlus) by a script-interpreter parent; console-less Python from Temp is atypical for legitimate deployed software. Cross-checked against: • https://socfortress.medium.com/acr-stealer-evolution-of-intrusion-chains-and-threat-activity-0052fb3dcc59
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1036.005 T1055
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate PyInstaller-style apps or dev tooling that unpack an embedded Python into a Temp dir
  • CI/build agents invoking pythonw from a temp working directory
  • Vendor telemetry agents bundling their own Python runtime under LocalAppData
  • Data-science users running notebook helpers from Temp
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !endswith "$" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("-enc", "IEX", "DownloadString", "FromBase64String", "Expand-Archive")
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the pythonw folder path and sibling files; look for an archive/installer masquerade, a bundled interpreter, and whether the parent PowerShell was the obfuscated loader. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill pythonw and any injected system process, and quarantine the Temp deceptive directory. 3) Hunt: check for VirtualAlloc/Fiber-API in-memory injection, DPAPI browser-store access, and the 'Autoupdate' scheduled task on the same and neighboring hosts.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "pythonw.exe"
| where FolderPath has @"\AppData\Local\Temp\"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "cmd.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\pythonw.exe"
| where NewProcessName has @"\AppData\Local\Temp\"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\powershell.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\cmd.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: ACR Stealer pythonw Loader from Temp Directory

Endpoint traffic to ACR Stealer C2 / dead-drop domains AICommand & Control High
Hunts outbound connections or DNS lookups to the corroborated ACR Stealer campaign infrastructure (creativecommunityinfo.art, enhanceblabber.cc, sphere-api.dialectosphere.in.net, looksta.icu, claude-desktop.gitlab.io) used for WebDAV payload staging and C2 resolution. Rationale: Pre-extracted campaign domains, with sphere-api.dialectosphere.in.net independently confirmed as the WebDAV staging host in external write-ups; direct IOC hits on these domains are high-fidelity for this campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://www.csoonline.com/article/4198788/new-acr-stealer-campaigns-use-webdav-mshta-to-evade-detection.html • https://blog.gridinsoft.com/acr-stealer-clickfix-attacks/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel feed crawler or sandbox in the environment resolving the IOC domains
  • Security researcher browsing the C2 domains from a corp host
  • Proxy/DNS logging replayed during IR that re-surfaces historical lookups
  • Domain sinkhole/monitoring service inside the org
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","SenseIR.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the initiating process for the connection/lookup (rundll32, pythonw, mshta, powershell) and confirm it is not a known security tool. 2) Contain: block all five domains at DNS+proxy, isolate any host that resolved them, and capture memory before reimage. 3) Hunt: pivot from the host to the full ACR chain (RunMRU paste, WebDAV rundll32 load, Autoupdate task, browser-credential access) and check for stolen-token reuse in Entra/M365 sign-in logs.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("creativecommunityinfo.art","enhanceblabber.cc","sphere-api.dialectosphere.in.net","looksta.icu","claude-desktop.gitlab.io")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let acrDomains = dynamic(["creativecommunityinfo.art","enhanceblabber.cc","sphere-api.dialectosphere.in.net","looksta.icu","claude-desktop.gitlab.io"]);
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DnsQuery has_any (acrDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
